title: Headhunter
subtitle: Jack Wade takes the case
summary: Headhunter is Amuze's action adventure, first released for Dreamcast in Europe on 16 November 2001.
body: Headhunter is Amuze's action adventure, first released for Dreamcast in Europe on 16 November 2001. The player follows Jack Wade, a bounty hunter in a near-future society where criminal punishment and a trade in human organs have become entwined. His investigation moves between armed confrontations and journeys across the city on a motorcycle. The setting resembles Los Angeles, giving the pursuit a recognisable action-film landscape. Jack's work brings that surface into contact with a harsher system beneath it, while the player's immediate task alternates between navigating the streets and surviving inside its buildings.

On foot, Jack uses third-person shooting and cover to work through hostile locations. The motorcycle connects those principal areas, changing the pace from cautious movement around enemies to travel through the city. Dreamcast's analogue triggers control acceleration and braking, allowing the player to adjust speed with pressure rather than a simple on-off input. Moving between these activities gives the city a role beyond a menu of missions. Reaching the next investigation becomes part of the action, with another set of controls and another kind of space to learn.

Richard Jacques composed the score, giving the pursuit a large-scale cinematic accompaniment. The game's electric weapons also belong to its premise: conventional guns have been replaced by technology intended to preserve the bodies of the people being hunted. That detail ties the equipment used in the encounters to the society Jack is investigating. A PlayStation 2 version followed in 2002, bringing the same adventure to another audience. On Dreamcast, its combination of motorcycle travel, shooting and orchestral presentation made it an ambitious late addition to the console's library.
